newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai and Abu Dhabi reach initial gas pact-MEES.
newsitem.headline: Dubai and Abu Dhabi reach initial gas pact-MEES.

text.p: Dubai appears to have reached initial agreement on long-term gas supplies from Abu Dhabi's offshore fields to its Jebel Ali industrial free zone, the Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) reported on Monday.
But details including price, volume, quality and timing "have yet to be definitively nailed down," the Cyprus-based weekly said.
Technical teams from Abu Dhabi National Oil Co ADNOC) and Dubai's Petroleum Department held their last meeting in October and it remains unclear when they expect to reach full agreement.

The emirate of Dubai, the trade and commercial heart of the United Arab Emirates, has to decide soon to guarantee future gas supplies as it takes up to three years to bring on stream new gas development projects, MEES said.

Dubai has relied on the emirate of Sharjah to meet most of its needs of around 500 million cubic feet daily (cfd) in recent years. But planners expect deliveries to decline within three to four years as its ageing gas fields are depleted.
Both sides also have to agree on volume, a sticking point, and on timing before they can look into pricing.

Abu Dhabi is offering 500 million cfd from end 1999. Dubai is pressing for full commitment to meet its expected 800 million cfd needs by the turn of the century and says it is ready to phase in the 300 million cfd once supplies start.

Local sources have suggested both might agree on a final price for dry sweetened gas delivered to Dubai's Jebel Ali at between 80 and 85 cents/million BTU though ADNOC has been supplying gas to its own electric power and water desalination plant at higher prices.
